column1: # Rule parameters for the food web. Change a value and rebuild.

column3: Burns 1968: largest particle um = slope x body length mm + intercept
fine mesh (Diaphanosoma, Ceriodaphnia, Chydorus, D. cucullata, D. magna). INTERPOLATED from Brendelberger's 0.2-4.7 um range, not a published class value
medium mesh (most Daphnia, Bosmina). INTERPOLATED, see above
coarse mesh (Holopedium, Sida). INTERPOLATED, see above
used where the mesh class is unknown, and for rotifers and copepods, which do not sieve like cladocerans: a placeholder

colonies at or above this size foul the filter rather than being eaten. OUR PLACEHOLDER: the effect is well established for filamentous cyanobacteria but we have not verified a published threshold. Filaments are excluded at any size, because the source standardises them to 100 um
raptorial feeders handle particles this many times larger than the Burns limit

largest prey a predator takes, as a fraction of its own body length
